messages.subject: Spatio temporal semicontinous model
parts:
Dear all,

I want to extend what has been done at section 5 of the manual "The R-INLA tutorial: SPDE models". Instead of restricting the analysis for only one day, I would like to fit a semicontinuous model, which is a mixture of Binomial and Gamma distributions, considering also the temporal component.

Just like in chapter 10 of the same material, I consider that the random effect is represented by a Random Field with Matern covariance function and across time it is modelled as a stationary process AR(1).

I believe that my problem is on how to define the "group" argument at the function for the random effect, which is used in the formula defined for the "inla" function.It has to be in accordance with the indices defined at the "effect" at the stack functionality when making the copy.

The way I defined it, as shown in the code below, I get an error message that the program was killed when trying to run inla.

As an example, I used the Rainfall data in the Parana state. Any input or advice would be appreciated. Let me know if I need to provide any additional information.

Thank you very much,

Amanda Lenzi

data(PRprec)
n_stations <- 616
times <- 365

z = matrix(c(NA), n_stations, times)
y = matrix(c(NA), n_stations, times)

for (i in 1:times){
  z[,i] = (PRprec[,3+i]>0) + 0
}

for (i in 1:times){
  y[,i] = ifelse(PRprec[,3+i]>0, PRprec[,3+i], NA)
}

# Define the mesh and the SPDE model
prdomain <- inla.nonconvex.hull(as.matrix(PRprec[,1:2]),
                                -0.03, -0.05, resolution=c(100,100))
mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(boundary=prdomain, max.edge=c(.45,1), cutoff=0.2)
spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh, alpha=2)

# Get the projector matrix for the SPDE model effect with
loc_utmx = as.vector(rep(PRprec[,1],times))
loc_utmy = as.vector(rep(PRprec[,2],times))

grupo = rep(1:times, each = n_stations)

A = inla.spde.make.A(mesh,
                     loc=as.matrix(cbind(loc_utmx, loc_utmy)),
                     group=grupo,
                     n.group = times)

# Creating index for the observations
field.indices_z =
  inla.spde.make.index("fieldz",
                       n.spde=spde$n.spde,
                       n.group=times)
field.indices_y =
  inla.spde.make.index("fieldy",
                       n.spde=spde$n.spde,
                       n.group=times)

# The stack for the occurrence and the amount
data_y = matrix(c(y), times*n_stations, 1)
data_z = matrix(c(z), times*n_stations, 1)

stk.z <- inla.stack(tag="est.z",
                    data=list(z=data_z, ### occurrence for separate model
                              y=cbind(data_z, NA)), ### z at first column of y
                    A=list(A, 1),
                    effects = list(
                            i.z=field.indices_z, z.b0=rep(1, length(data_z))))

stk.y <- inla.stack(tag="est.y",
                    data=list(r=data_y, ### amount for separate model
                              y=cbind(NA, data_y)), ### amount at second column of y
                    A=list(A, 1),
                    effects = list(
                      i.y=field.indices_y, y.b0=rep(1, length(data_y))))

#Defining a full data stack that join both responses for jointly model
stk.zy <- inla.stack(stk.z, stk.y)

#Defining the formula and run INLA
formula_zy <- (y ~ 0 + z.b0 + y.b0 +
                 f(fieldz, model=spde, group=fieldz.group,
                   control.group=list(model="ar1"))
               + f(fieldy, copy="fieldz", fixed=FALSE) )

res.zy <- inla(formula_zy,
               family=c('binomial', 'gamma'),
               data=inla.stack.data(stk.zy, spde=spde),
               control.compute=list(dic=TRUE),
               control.inla = list(h = 1e-6),
               verbose=TRUE,
               control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stk.zy), compute=TRUE))
